en.title: 'Tis So Sweet to Trust in Jesus
en.author: Louisa M. R. Stead
stanzas:
[G]'Tis so sweet to [C]trust in [G]Jesus,
Just to take Him [D]at His Word;
[G]Just to rest up[C]on His [G]promise,
Just to [C]know, "Thus [D]saith the [G]Lord!"

Oh, how sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just to trust His cleansing blood;
And in simple faith to plunge me
'Neath the healing, cleansing flood!

Yes, 'tis sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just from sin and self to cease;
Just from Jesus simply taking
Life and rest, and joy and peace.

I'm so glad I learned to trust Thee,
Precious Jesus, Savior, Friend;
And I know that Thou art with me,
Wilt be with me to the end.
en.chorus:
[G]Jesus, Jesus, [D7]how I [G]trust [D]Him!
[G]How I've proved Him [D]o'er and o'er;
[G]Jesus, Jesus, [C]precious [G]Jesus!
Oh, for [C]grace to [D]trust Him [G]more!

notes: Text from Timeless Truths, with one correction from TT's own score: TT's text page prints stanza 1 line 4 as 'And to know', but the lyric under the notes in its MusicXML reads 'Just to know', which is the 1882 reading and the one the Cyber Hymnal prints; the score is followed. Hymnary's representative text (United Methodist Hymnal #462) is a modernised three-stanza version ('and to take him at his word', lower-case pronouns, stanza 4 dropped) and was NOT followed; its notes confirm four stanzas. Tune TRUST IN JESUS (Kirkpatrick), meter 8.7.8.7 with refrain. Key: hymnary's instances run 40 G to 25 A-flat; TT prints A-flat. G is both the commoner hymnal key and a guitar key, so the chart is in G and the A-flat score was transposed down a semitone. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat, transposed A-flat to G. Stanza: I, IV (with its /E and /G inversions walking the bass, dropped), I; 'at His Word' is V with a II7/E approach dropped; line 4 IV-V-I. Refrain bar 2 is V7-vi-I6/4-V under 'how I trust Him', written V7-I-V; the 6/4 under 'trust' is the only I in the bar.
